identity.title: Dynamical Decoupling of Generalization and Overfitting in Large Two-Layer Networks

problem.claim: Characterize how training dynamics determine inductive bias and generalization in large overparameterized models.

contributions.claim: Analyzes learning dynamics of large two-layer networks using dynamical mean field theory.
Reports a separation of timescales linking complexity growth, inductive bias, feature learning, and overfitting.
Identifies a late-time feature-unlearning regime associated with non-monotone test error.

stated_novelty.claim: The reported dynamical decoupling between feature learning and overfitting is presented as a characteristic of the training dynamics in the stated large-width and high-sample regimes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, for large width m and large n/d, training dynamics exhibit separated timescales, including a slow scale associated with increasing Gaussian/Rademacher complexity.
They report an inductive bias toward small complexity when initialization has sufficiently small complexity.
They report non-monotone test error and feature unlearning at large times.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames training dynamics as necessary for understanding inductive bias and generalization in large overparameterized models.
Studies large two-layer-network dynamics through dynamical mean field theory.
Reports separated timescales, complexity-related inductive bias, decoupled feature learning and overfitting, and late-time feature unlearning with non-monotone test error.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates several training phenomena by timescale and explicitly connects them to complexity, feature learning, overfitting, and test-error behavior.

lessons.interpretation: A timescale-based framing can make relationships among training phases and generalization behavior more mechanistic and testable.
lessons.application: When presenting a dynamics result, organize claims by timescale and state which observable or regime each timescale explains.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the method or data do not support distinct temporal regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative timescales, theorem statements, finite-width or finite-sample conditions beyond the asymptotic regime, or empirical validation details.
